layman_headline: Fear dominates crypto markets — no good swing trade setups right now.
layman_explanation: The crypto market is in a fearful mood with Bitcoin down about 2% over the past week and most altcoins down even more. While a couple of coins show oversold readings that might suggest a bounce, the overall market structure is bearish with high Bitcoin dominance squeezing altcoins. A Coldcard wallet exploit worth $89 million is rattling confidence and distorting market signals — not the environment for confident entries.
layman_action: Stay patient with cash on hand. Wait for the fear to either peak and reverse (look for Fear & Greed dropping below 20 then bouncing back above 30) or for a clear technical setup with volume confirmation before committing capital.
expert_reasoning: I evaluated all seven swing candidates against validated rules and signal credibility data. TRUMP has the best RSI reading (27 — oversold, and RSI is my most reliable signal at 71% win rate), but the chart bias is -0.70 with poor risk/reward (0.67x) and price below all MAs. Per swing trading principles, a good setup needs clear downside limits and favorable risk/reward. DEXE's -30.4% weekly drop suggests mean reversion potential, but Three Black Crows pattern with -1.40 chart bias indicates selling is accelerating. WLD offers the best risk/reward at 4.35x, but its 5-day momentum is -19% despite being labeled 'uptrend,' creating conflicting signals. Fear & Greed at 27 is near the 25 threshold where my Rule #3 says the outlook is genuinely ambiguous. BTC dominance at 56.2% actively suppresses altcoin recovery. With no funding rate data, no MACD crosses confirmed, and most chart biases negative, the responsible call is HOLD.

market_context: Crypto markets are in a fear-driven consolidation with BTC at $63,310 and dominance at 56.2%. The Coldcard exploit and Trump Media BTC sales are adding negative pressure, while most altcoins are down 5-30% over the past week.
context_banner: Market fear is elevated with no high-conviction swing setups — capital preservation is the priority until conditions improve.
